entry.title: Steve Vai-Owned 1999 Ibanez JEM7D Prototype Guitar Available For Sale at The Music Zoo
entry.summary:
An Ibanez JEM7D with a Black Textured finish which traveled with Steve Vai on the 1999 Ultra Zone World Tour as a warm-up instrument is available for sale at The Music Zoo!

More
entry.content:
An Ibanez JEM7D with a Black Textured finish which traveled with Steve Vai on the 1999 Ultra Zone World Tour as a warm-up instrument is available for sale at The Music Zoo!

This special guitar is an Ibanez Steve Vai JEM 7D prototype with that models signature 'Black Textured' finish. What makes the guitar special is that this prototype traveled around with world with Steve Vai on the 1999-2000 Ultra Zone tour where he favored it as his instrument to warm up with back stage and play in hotel rooms. For someone as gifted as Steve Vai and particular with gear, there must be a connection he had with this guitar for it to travel with him and get him ready to perform on stage.

The guitar went on to be gifted to a member of the touring crew, and years later is now available for sale. The guitar includes a letter of authenticity written and signed by Steve Vai himself, as well as Steve's favored DiMarzio Clip-Lok strap setup and five picks on the headstock, too! A wonderful instrument to add to the collection of any fan of Steve Vai and his incredible music.

More
entry.content:
Fender Custom Shop Just Released a Limited Run of the George Harrison 1967 Bass VI! Pre-Orders are available now at The Music Zoo! Watch the video and see pics below.

About the new Fender Custom Shop Limited Edition George Harrison 1967 Bass VI Guitar

Available only at Fender Custom Shop Showcase Dealers like The Music Zoo, this Limited to 100 piece run is a painstaking recreation of George Harrisons iconic instrument.

George Harrison’s sunburst Fender® Bass VI became an essential voice at Abbey Road Studios, providing the melodic counterpoints and textural layers that shaped some of the most admired arrangements in popular music. 

The two-piece select alder body delivers resonant warmth and balanced midrange, with a thin nitrocellulose lacquer finish. The Relic® treatment in Bleached 3-Color Sunburst gives this bass the worn-in look and feel of an instrument that has seen years of regular studio and stage use.

The neck is shaped to match the profile of Harrison’s Bass VI, featuring a bound 3A rosewood fingerboard and white pearloid block inlays. The 7.25” radius and 21 vintage frets provide the period-correct playing surface that rewards a lighter touch with expressive dynamics, making chord voicings and melodic runs feel effortless across the 30” scale length. This shorter scale produces inherently lower string tension, lending a supple, elastic feel that invites both bass lines and guitar-style phrasing. A bone nut ensures precise intonation and open-string sustain at the headstock end.

 


George Harrison Bass VI Specs

  • 2-Piece Select Alder
  • Relic® Nitrocellulose Lacquer
  • Bleached 3-Color Sunburst
  • 4-Ply Brown Shell Pickguard
  • Maple with 1960 Oval “C” Back-Shape
  • 3A Rosewood, 7.25” Radius with 21, Vintage Frets
  • White Pearloid Block Inlays
  • Bone, 1.5” (38.1 mm) Nut
  • Custom Shop Hand-Wound Flat Magnet Jaguar® Pickups
  • Master Volume, Master Tone
  • 3-On/Off Slide Switches (One for Each Pickup)
  • 2-Position Slide Switch for Bass-Cut “Strangle” Circuit
  • 6-Saddle Vintage-Style Adjustable w/ “Floating” Tremolo Tailpiece with Bass VI Mute Bridge

entry.content:
From playing in Metal bands to taking apart original 1959 Les Pauls and guitar teching for Slash and Joe Bonamassa - Mike Hickey has seen and played it all! Watch our video interview now!

For Episode Two of our new Music Zoo Series 'Electric History' - Music Zoo founder and owner Tommy Colletti speaks to his longtime friend Mike Hickey - a shredder with a long history on stage and off! Mike has playedg with bands such as Cronos and Venom who has then gone on to be a guitar tech traveling with Joe Bonamassa and Slash among many others. He's also a key figure behind the scenes who has helped many source vintage gear, and has seen possibly more authentic 1950s Gibson Les Pauls, Flying V's and Explorers than any other person on the planet. Mike is a true guitar historian and it was a pleasure to speak with him!

entry.title: In Memoriam: Wayne Charvel, a Pioneer of the Guitar Industry.
entry.summary:
Memories of Wayne Charvel, famed luthier and founder of Charvel Guitars by Music Zoo Owner Tommy Colletti

The guitar world recently lost one of its true pioneers with the passing of Wayne Charvel.

For many people, Wayne’s name is forever attached to the Charvel brand and the guitars that helped define an era of rock music. But I had the privilege of knowing Wayne beyond the logo on a headstock. To me, he was one of the kindest, most genuine people I’ve met in over three decades in the guitar business.

More
entry.content:
Memories of Wayne Charvel, famed luthier and founder of Charvel Guitars by Music Zoo Owner Tommy Colletti

The guitar world recently lost one of its true pioneers with the passing of Wayne Charvel.

For many people, Wayne’s name is forever attached to the Charvel brand and the guitars that helped define an era of rock music. But I had the privilege of knowing Wayne beyond the logo on a headstock. To me, he was one of the kindest, most genuine people I’ve met in over three decades in the guitar business.

The Music Zoo has been a longtime Charvel dealer, but years after Wayne sold the original Charvel company, we also became dealers for Wayne Guitars. That relationship eventually led me to visit Wayne and his son Michael at their shop in Paradise, California, in the early 2000s and I'll never forget that trip. 

I spent a weekend with Wayne and Michael, and they couldn’t have been more gracious. Their workshop sat in one of the most beautiful places imaginable. Looking out the shop windows, all you could see were towering pines, forests, deer wandering by, and the incredible scenery that gave Paradise its name. It was peaceful, inspiring, and exactly where you’d imagine a master craftsman creating guitars by hand.

Wayne’s shop reflected who he was. It wasn’t about flash or marketing. It was about building the best guitars he possibly could, and that's exactly what he did.

To this day, I still believe Wayne produced some of the finest-playing guitars I’ve ever had in my hands. His setups were simply extraordinary. Every guitar played effortlessly. There was something about the way he approached geometry, fretwork, neck angles, and setup that made his instruments disappear beneath your hands. They didn’t fight you—they encouraged you to play.

Wayne was endlessly curious. We’d spend time talking about music, guitars, woodworking, life, and ideas that most people would never even think about. One conversation that has stayed with me all these years was about how we actually hear music. Wayne talked about how our sinuses, our turbinates, and even how we felt on a given day could change the way we perceived tone. Depending on your body, your mood, or simply the day itself, you might hear the same guitar differently.

He didn’t just build guitars—he thought deeply about why we connected with them. He was the definition of a Renaissance man. If he wasn’t building guitars, he could probably build the shop they were made in. If something mechanical broke, he could fix it. Whether it was woodworking, machinery, cars, or guitars, Wayne seemed capable of doing almost anything with his hands.

Yet despite all that knowledge, he never carried himself like someone who wanted recognition. He was always calm, thoughtful and willing to lend a helping hand. Most importantly, he loved his family. 

In many ways, Wayne was more passionate about the craft than he ever was about the business. Something most don't know... in the late '90s and early 2000's, Edward Van Halen approached Wayne before he went to Fender to build replicas of the Frankenstein for production. Wayne passed on the idea because he didn't want to hire a bunch of people and ramp up the stress that large-scale guitar manufacturing could cause later in his life. Edward then went to Fender and started the relationship that still goes on as the EVH brand.

That authenticity came through in every instrument he built and every conversation we shared. Whenever I needed advice over the years, Wayne was always generous with his time. He never made you feel like you were interrupting him. He simply wanted to help.

The guitar industry has been fortunate to have many talented builders, but there are only a handful of true innovators who leave a permanent mark on the instruments we play today. Wayne Charvel was unquestionably one of them. His influence can be seen not only in the guitars that bear his name, but throughout the entire high-performance electric guitar world.

I’m grateful that our paths crossed and I'm grateful that I got to visit his shop. Most of all, I’m grateful that I got to know Wayne not just as a legendary builder, but as a genuinely wonderful human being.

My heartfelt condolences go out to Michael, the twins, his wife, his daughter, and everyone who loved him. I know this is an incredibly difficult time.

Wayne’s guitars will continue to inspire musicians for generations to come, but those of us who were lucky enough to know the man will remember something even more important.

We’ll remember his kindness.

Rest in peace, Wayne. Thank you for everything.

-Tommy Colletti

entry.content:
An original 1959 Gibson Les Paul - one of the most prestigious electric guitar models of all time is being offered for sale at The Music Zoo!


The Music Zoo is proud to offer this incredible, all-original 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard for sale. This guitar bears the serial number 90320, with a wonderful Sunburst finish that has retained most of its color through more than six decades. Before it was in the collection of its previous owner, the guitar was sourced from a private collection where it resided for many years - helping to maintain its excellent condition. The 'Patent Applied For' Gibson humbuckers are original as is the internal wiring harness, and all original hardware including the tuners, plastics, bridge, and tailpiece.

Shop All Les Pauls Available For Sale at The Music Zoo!


With only 643 Sunburst Les Pauls made in 1959, used by legends such as Jimmy Page, Peter Green, Mike Bloomfield, Eric Clapton and Billy Gibbons, the 1959 Les Paul remains an iconic guitar and an excellent long-term investment.

 Considering its age, originality, and level of preservation, this is an excellent example of a 1959 Les Paul. There is lots of red left in the burst, with the most fading into lighter colors on the bass side of the top. The most distinctive visual characteristic is the concentrated fading on the upper bass-side edge running along the fretboard. The fretboard retains the original frets, which, accurate to what Gibson used at the time, are quite small compared to modern frets but still have lots of life remaining. There is a light amount of worming on the back of the body, a few small dents on the maple top, and some wear to the top edges of the back of the headstock. The holly veneer and Gibson logo remain in excellent condition, as does the neck with nothing beyond finish fading. This Les Paul weighs 8 lbs, 6 oz. The neck measures .880" at the first fret and .990" at the 12th fret.

entry.content:
New features on Taylor Next Generation guitars include V-Class Scalloped bracing, the Action Control neck joint and Taylor Claria electronics - now expanded to new models for 2026!

Huge news, Taylor has expanded the "Next Generation" of their Standard Collection of guitars which have three updates; Action Controls Necks, V-Class Scalloped bracing and Claria electronics. Our friend from Taylor, Mike Venezia stopped by to help us understand the how and why Taylor brought about these changes, and we're talking about it in an easy way: we're learning our Taylor ABCs.

First debuting on the Gold Label Collection in 2025, the Action Control neck is now available on Next Generation Standard Collection guitars such as these! The long-tenon neck joint improved the neck to body connection while also making adjusting your action easier than ever. With the use of a simple tool - you can adjust your action on the fly without the need to take off your strings. A quick adjustment on the fly can make a big difference during a performance or recording session.

The scalloped V-Class bracing unlocks a warmer low-end and a richer open-string resonance while preserving the balance and pitch-accuracy we know and love V-Class bracing for.

Taylor's new Claria active electronics system is powered by an under-saddle piezo pickup with a proprietary pre-amp which tames the sometimes harsh sounds of a piezo pickup. The controls are now mounted within the soundhole as opposed to the outside of the upper bout; Volume, Tone, and a Mid-Contour control allow you to really dial in your amplifier sound!
